assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data changed how intergenerational mobility is measured. It also showed that childhood place and neighbourhood exposure causally matter, which fed directly into policy debate. The work is broad in method (quasi-experimental, big data) and applied to questions central to economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the mobility and neighbourhood-effects results (Opportunity Atlas, exposure effects). Friedman and Katz are important co-authors, but a two-person core is cleanest. The credit boundary with the broader Opportunity Insights team is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from about 2014 to 2022, with follow-up replication and use in policy. Impact is already large, but the long-run durability of some neighbourhood-effect estimates is still being tested.
uncertainties: How much weight to give to the empirical-measurement contribution versus conceptual novelty
Whether the committee prefers a more established, older cohort of candidates
Possible undervaluing of earlier mobility literature, such as Solon and Corak, not on this list

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock research gave credible local-labour-market evidence on the distributional costs of trade. It reshaped both the trade and labour fields and public policy discussion. The empirical identification strategy is influential and widely replicated.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are clearly the core authors of the trade-shock papers. Task-based labour demand is a separate strand that overlaps with Acemoglu, who is already recognised. Katz is more peripheral here.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from 2013 to 2016 and have had a decade of replication and extension. The literature is mature, and the debate about magnitudes has become more nuanced rather than overturning the main finding.
uncertainties: Persistence and magnitude of the effects under alternative specifications
Overlap with the 2024 prize on technology and institutions
Whether the committee sees the contribution as primarily empirical application

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade theory (Melitz 2003, with Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple) is the dominant framework for modern trade and the foundation of a large empirical literature. It explains selection, productivity gains and the intensive and extensive margins of trade. Its effect on the field is large and clearly deserves recognition.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the main originator of the model. Helpman broadened the framework (exports versus FDI, labour-market frictions) and earlier shaped new trade theory. Redding is important in quantitative extensions but is a later-generation contributor. Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are important antecedents who are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of theoretical development and empirical testing. The framework has been integrated into policy evaluation models.
uncertainties: Credit split with Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, who are outside this candidate's credited names
Overlap with the Krugman new-trade-theory prize of 2008
Pairing with Helpman's related work on trade policy (B043)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is the canonical model of how collateral constraints and asset prices amplify and propagate shocks, and it is a foundation of modern macro-finance. It explains credit cycles and the transmission of financial shocks. It was highly relevant after 2008 and is a conceptual advance, not only an application.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint cycle mechanism. Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist is a related financial accelerator line, and Gilchrist and Gertler have related but distinct credit. Bernanke is already a laureate, which complicates the broader framing.
assessment.maturity: Close to 30 years of influence, with extensive extensions in macro, banking and quantitative models. Its standing is very well established.
uncertainties: How the committee would treat the earlier Bernanke recognition when framing the financial accelerator
Whether a narrow pairing fully captures the field
Empirical validation is more indirect than for some other candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) provided a tractable way to measure misallocation across firms and its aggregate cost. It reframed cross-country income differences as partly an allocation problem and is among the most used tools in development and growth accounting. It has strong policy relevance and strong methodological reach.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the core authors of the measurement framework. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) developed parallel and earlier theoretical insight, but Rogerson is not credited here. The credit boundary is somewhat sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years of use and refinement. There is a live debate about measurement error, adjustment costs and whether dispersion truly reflects distortions.
uncertainties: Concerns about measurement error and the interpretation of TFP dispersion as misallocation
Priority issues with Restuccia and Rogerson
Whether the contribution is viewed as primarily methodological

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income series built from tax records transformed the empirical study of inequality and brought it to the centre of the field. Related work on wealth concentration and its dynamics shaped public debate. The data-construction contribution is lasting, although the theoretical claims about wealth dynamics have drawn criticism.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the founders of the top-income series (with Atkinson, who is deceased). Zucman is a later contributor on offshore wealth and distributional accounts. Credit should rest on the data-construction contribution, not on contested theoretical claims.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of data work. The conceptual claims about r>g and wealth dynamics are still debated, which tempers the assessment.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of the wealth-dynamics and capital-income claims
Atkinson's deceased status affects attribution
Possible perception of policy advocacy

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework underlies how central banks think about inflation and stabilisation policy. Calvo pricing, the NK Phillips curve and the microfounded monetary policy analysis are foundational and have clear practical influence.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many people: Calvo (price setting), Taylor (policy rules), Galí and Woodford (the canonical framework), and Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans and Smets-Wouters (medium-scale estimation). Any three-person selection necessarily leaves out major contributors, which is a significant weakness.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with 25 or more years of influence. Challenges after the financial crisis and the inflation episode of 2021 to 2023 prompted refinements instead of replacement.
uncertainties: Credit fragmentation and an arbitrary cut at three names
Debate about how well the framework performed in recent inflation
Overlap with earlier recognition of the rational expectations and monetary policy literature

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A systematic formal and empirical programme on how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It created modern political economics as a field and links well to growth and development. The empirical identification of constitutional effects is harder, but the conceptual contribution is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central figures in constitutional political economics. Besley is the leading figure on state capacity, accountability and the political economy of development. Credit is shared closely among the three, and Acemoglu-Robinson are already recognised for adjacent institutional work.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of work with many follow-ups. The empirical identification of effects of electoral rules and constitutions remains partly contested.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity
Causal identification for cross-country constitutional effects
Whether the contribution is seen as a field or as a single discovery
